
Renders everything about a type beyond its declaration: the traits it implements (from every file), its functions grouped by receiver, the functions those traits provide, and the other modules that add functions to it.

### `companionIndexHtml`

```kex
companionIndexHtml(name: String, page: SourcePage) -> String
```

Lists the functions of the module named like the type, such as `Set.from` and `Set.empty`, at the top of the type's summary. That module's own section comes much further down the page, and its functions are how a reader gets a `Set` in the first place.

Returns `true` when a group has six or more function names and so opens with an index: each name with the first sentence of its doc, linked to its entry. A shorter group needs no index.

Returns `true` when `target` is the type itself with type parameters, such as `[X]` or `FileHandle<R, W>`, and not a specialisation such as `[Number]`.

### `functionsHtml`


Renders the functions of a trait or make block, one heading per name, so overloads such as `count` and `count(pred)` appear as one function with several signatures. `owner` scopes the anchors, and `implements` lets a function that fulfils a trait say which trait.


### `memberHeadHtml`

```kex

```

Renders the head of a member's card: its signature with the heading's chips beside it, in one row, so a long signature scrolls in its own space without running under them. A stylesheet may still float the permalink, which appears only on hover. A member with no type is headed by its name in the same way, so every card has the same shape.

### `traitTag`


Returns the "from Enumerable" tag for a member that is the type's own version of a trait function, linked to the trait's entry for it.


Wraps one signature in an element of its own, so a stylesheet can treat each overload as a unit.

### `namedFirst`

```kex
namedFirst(html: String, name: String) -> String
```

Marks the name that opens a signature as a name. The highlighter alone marks it as a function only when a parameter list follows, so `count : Integer` would come out plain beside `count(pred)`, and a function called `from` or `in` would be coloured as a keyword.

Renders the permalink beside a heading: a link to its own anchor, which the page script turns into a "copy this address" control.

package: tey
version: "0.2.1-dev"

title: Tey.Docgen.Index
entities:
  - { kind: module, name: "Tey.Docgen.Index" }

# Tey.Docgen.Index

The `tey docs build` driver. It scans and extracts the sources into a `PackageModel`, then writes everything derived from it: model.json, search.json, the Markdown pages, and either the HTML site (with its manifests, versions.json, llms.txt, llms-full.txt, robots.txt and sitemap.xml) or, with `--format fragments`, HTML fragments for a host site.

## module `Tey.Docgen.Index`

### `buildCommand` (foul)

```kex
buildCommand(parsed: ParsedOptions) -> Integer
```

### `externalLinks` (foul)

```kex
externalLinks(paths: String) -> [LinkEntry]
```

Returns the names documented by other units, read from the comma-separated model.json files in `paths`, so this unit's signatures and prose can link to them.

The Tey reference uses this to link `String` and `FS.Path` to the standard library. Each model.json names its package and version, and its pages are linked at ../../<package>/<version>/ from this unit's version directory. A file that cannot be read or is not JSON is reported as a warning and skipped.

### `writeUnitIndexFiles` (foul)

```kex
writeUnitIndexFiles(pages: [SourcePage], model: PackageModel, out: String) -> ()
```

Writes this unit's version manifest and the shared versions.json, but none of the site-wide files (landing pages, llms.txt, sitemap), which belong to the host site that embeds the fragments.

### `reportDocDrift` (foul)

```kex
reportDocDrift(pages: [SourcePage]) -> ()
```

Prints a note for each `@return` tag whose type differs from the signature's, such as `min : X?` documented as returning `Number?`.

The page shows the signature's type either way; the note says which comment has fallen behind its code.

### `normalizeType`

```kex
normalizeType(text: String) -> String
```

### `optString`

```kex
optString(value: String?) -> String
```

### `preludeInfo` (foul)

```kex
preludeInfo(source: String) -> (String, [String], String)
```

Returns the prelude of the source tree at `source`: the file name, the modules it makes visible, and its opening comment.

A `prelude.kex` is an opening comment followed by one bare `using <Module>` per line, so reading the lines is enough. Without one the result is `("", [], "")` and the output never mentions a prelude.

### `leadingComment`

```kex
leadingComment(lines: [String]) -> String
```

Returns the comment lines at the top of `lines` with their `#` markers removed, ready for the same parse as any other doc comment.

### `commentBody`

```kex
commentBody(line: String) -> String
```

### `fileHeader`

```kex
fileHeader(lines: [String]) -> String
```

Returns the file's opening comment when a blank line follows it, and `""` otherwise.

A comment that runs straight into a declaration is that declaration's doc, and the page gets no introduction. A `#!` line does not count as a comment.

### `usingName`

```kex
usingName(line: String) -> String
```

Returns the module a `using` line names (`"using List"` gives `"List"`), or `""` for any other line.

### `defaultSource` (foul)

```kex
defaultSource(given: String) -> String
```

Returns `given` when it is not empty, else `"src"` when the current directory has one, else `""`, which the scan reports as having no .kex files.

### `defaultPackage` (foul)

```kex
defaultPackage(given: String) -> String
```

Returns `given` when it is not empty, else the name in the current directory's package.kex, else `""`.

With `""`, `buildCommand` stops with an error and asks for `--package`; it does not invent a name (kexhq/kex#287).

### `defaultVersion` (foul)

```kex
defaultVersion(given: String) -> String
```

Returns `given` when it is not empty, else the version in the current directory's package.kex, else `""`.

Outside a package the caller must pass `--release`: what a version means differs between units, such as a library's releases and the standard library's Kex releases.

### `manifestVersion` (foul)

```kex
manifestVersion -> (String, String)?
```

Returns the name and version from the current directory's package.kex, or `None` when there is none or it does not parse.

### `buildPages` (foul)

```kex
buildPages(files: [String], sourceDir: String) -> [SourcePage]
```

### `buildPagesLoop` (foul)

```kex
buildPagesLoop(files: [String], sourceDir: String, pages: [SourcePage]) -> [SourcePage]
```

### `writePages` (foul)

```kex
writePages(pages: [SourcePage], versionDir: String, model: PackageModel) -> Integer
```

### `writeHtml` (foul)

```kex
writeHtml(pages: [SourcePage], versionDir: String, out: String, model: PackageModel) -> ()
```

Writes the HTML site for one version: a page per source file, the version's index.html and search.html, and the shared assets/style.css and assets/site.js.

### `dirNameOf`

```kex
dirNameOf(urlPath: String) -> String
```

Returns the directory part of a page's URL path: `"kex/ast"` gives `"kex"`, and `"fs"` gives `""`.

### `ensureDirectory` (foul)

```kex
ensureDirectory(path: String) -> ()
```

### `writeIndexFiles` (foul)

```kex
writeIndexFiles(pages: [SourcePage], model: PackageModel, out: String) -> ()
```

### `versionManifestJson`

```kex
versionManifestJson(pages: [SourcePage], model: PackageModel) -> String
```

Returns the manifest.json for one version: its package, version, label, build time and pages.

Page paths are relative to the version directory, `<package>/<version>/`; whoever assembles the site adds the site root.

### `manifestJson`

```kex
manifestJson(pages: [SourcePage]) -> String
```

### `accumulateVersions` (foul)

```kex
accumulateVersions(out: String, model: PackageModel) -> [VersionEntry]
```

Returns the versions.json entries with this build's added.

The output directory is the published site, so other builds' versions are kept: the existing entries are read, this package and version replaces any earlier entry for it, and this build comes first.

### `upsertVersion`

```kex
upsertVersion(current: VersionEntry, existing: [VersionEntry]) -> [VersionEntry]
```

Returns `existing` with any entry for the same package and version removed and `current` put first.

package: tey
version: "0.2.1-dev"
source: tey/docgen/json.kex
title: Tey.Docgen.Json
entities:
  - { kind: module, name: "Tey.Docgen.Json" }
---

# Tey.Docgen.Json

Renders the documentation model as JSON: `model.json`, the full model, and `search.json`, a flat index for searching the docs site by name, kind and type.

This is the only place where the typed model records are turned into plain maps with atom keys, ready for `JSON.stringify`.

## module `Tey.Docgen.Json`

### `modelJson`

```kex
modelJson(model: PackageModel) -> String
```

### `moduleIndexValue`

```kex
moduleIndexValue(m: Tey.Docgen.Model.ModuleIndexEntry) -> Any
```

### `linkValue`

```kex
linkValue(l: Tey.Docgen.Model.LinkEntry) -> Any
```

### `labelOrPackage`

```kex
labelOrPackage(model: PackageModel) -> String
```

### `pageValue`

```kex
pageValue(page: SourcePage) -> Any
```

### `entityValue`

```kex
entityValue(e: Entity) -> Any
```

### `variantsValue`

```kex
variantsValue(variants: [VariantEntry]?) -> Any
```

### `fieldValue`

```kex
fieldValue(f: FieldEntry) -> Any
```

### `fieldValues`

```kex
fieldValues(fields: [FieldEntry]) -> Any
```

A named helper so the lambda's element type comes from the [FieldEntry] parameter, not from the surrounding map literal's value type.

### `functionValue`

```kex
functionValue(f: FunctionEntry) -> Any
```

### `docValue`

```kex

```

### `returnsValue`



### `searchEntries`


### `pageSearchEntries`

```kex
pageSearchEntries(page: SourcePage) -> [SearchEntry]
```

### `entitySearchEntries`

```kex
entitySearchEntries(e: Entity, page: SourcePage) -> [SearchEntry]
```

### `entityTypes`

```kex
entityTypes(e: Entity) -> [String]
```

Returns the type names an entity is about, for search by type: a function's signature types, a record's field types, a type's parents and variant fields, the types a trait's or make block's functions mention, and for a module the union of its children's.

### `variantFieldTypes`


package: tey
version: "0.2.1-dev"
source: tey/docgen/md.kex
title: Tey.Docgen.Md
entities:
  - { kind: module, name: "Tey.Docgen.Md" }
---

# Tey.Docgen.Md

A Markdown reader: parses a document into blocks and renders them as HTML, so hand-written pages get the same layout as the generated reference.

(`Tey.Docgen.Markdown` goes the other way, writing Markdown from the model.)

It reads the subset the kex.run guide pages use: simple `key: value` frontmatter, `#` headings, paragraphs, fenced code (`kex` code is highlighted), blockquotes, nested ordered and unordered lists, GFM tables, horizontal rules, and inline code, bold, italics and links. It is not CommonMark: there is no inline HTML, no reference links and no underlined headings. Anything it does not recognise is a paragraph, never an error.

## module `Tey.Docgen.Md`

### `parseDocument`

```kex
parseDocument(text: String) -> Document
```

Parses a Markdown document. Windows line endings are accepted.

### `toHtml`

```kex
toHtml(text: String) -> String
```

Returns the HTML for a document's body, ignoring its frontmatter.

### `splitFrontmatter`

```kex
splitFrontmatter(lines: [String]) -> (Frontmatter, [String])
```

--- frontmatter -------------------------------------------------------

A leading `---` fence delimits frontmatter. Without one the document is all body, and every field takes its default.

### `closingFence`

```kex
closingFence(lines: [String], index: Integer) -> Integer?
```

### `frontmatterOf`

```kex
frontmatterOf(lines: [String], accum: Frontmatter) -> Frontmatter
```

### `assign`

```kex
assign(front: Frontmatter, key: String, value: String) -> Frontmatter
```

### `unquote`

```kex
unquote(value: String) -> String
```

### `trimEnds`

```kex
trimEnds(value: String) -> String
```

Drops the first and last character, the quotes `quoted?` matched.

### `quoted?`

```kex
quoted?(value: String, mark: String) -> Bool
```

### `parseBlocks`

```kex
parseBlocks(lines: [String]) -> [MdBlock]
```

--- block structure ---------------------------------------------------

### `blockLoop`

```kex
blockLoop(lines: [String], accum: [MdBlock]) -> [MdBlock]
```

One pass over the lines, each branch consuming the whole construct it recognises and returning the lines it did not take.

### `fence?`

```kex
fence?(line: String) -> Bool
```

### `rule?`

```kex
rule?(line: String) -> Bool
```

Returns `true` for a horizontal rule: three or more of `-`, `*` or `_` and nothing else on the line. Frontmatter is removed before this runs.

### `ruleOf?`

```kex
ruleOf?(text: String, mark: String) -> Bool
```

### `headingLevel`

```kex
headingLevel(line: String) -> Integer
```

Returns a heading's level, so `##` gives 2, or 0 when the line is not a heading. `#hashtag` is not one.

### `countHashes`

```kex
countHashes(text: String, seen: Integer) -> Integer
```

### `takeCode`

```kex
takeCode(lines: [String]) -> (MdBlock, [String])
```

--- fenced code -------------------------------------------------------

Takes a fenced code block. The word after the fence is the language. A fence that is never closed runs to the end of the document.

### `closingCodeFence`

```kex
closingCodeFence(lines: [String], index: Integer) -> Integer
```

### `takeQuote`

```kex
takeQuote(lines: [String]) -> (MdBlock, [String])
```

--- blockquotes -------------------------------------------------------

Takes a blockquote. The `>` is stripped from each line and the rest is parsed as blocks, so a quote can hold anything a document can.

### `quoteLine?`

```kex
quoteLine?(line: String) -> Bool
```

### `stripQuote`

```kex
stripQuote(line: String) -> String
```

### `takeList`

```kex
takeList(lines: [String]) -> (MdBlock, [String])
```

--- lists -------------------------------------------------------------

Takes a list. A line indented past the first item's marker belongs to the item above it and is parsed as blocks, so an item can hold paragraphs, code and nested lists.

### `listLine?`

```kex
listLine?(line: String) -> Bool
```

Returns `true` for a line that can continue a list: an item, an indented line or a blank line. The first other line ends the list.

### `listItems`

```kex
listItems(lines: [String], indent: Integer, current: [String], accum: [ListItem]) -> [ListItem]
```

### `flushItem`

```kex
flushItem(current: [String], accum: [ListItem]) -> [ListItem]
```

Adds the collected item to `accum`. The first line is the item's text; the lines below it are dedented and parsed as nested blocks.

### `dropTrailingBlanks`

```kex
dropTrailingBlanks(lines: [String]) -> [String]
```

### `dedent`

```kex
dedent(lines: [String]) -> [String]
```

Removes the common indent, so nested content is parsed at column zero.

### `indentOf`

```kex
indentOf(line: String) -> Integer
```

### `itemMarker`

```kex
itemMarker(line: String) -> String
```

### `bulletMarker`

```kex
bulletMarker(line: String) -> String
```

### `numberMarker`

```kex
numberMarker(line: String) -> String
```

Returns a numbered-list marker, so `"12. "` gives `"12."`, or `""` when the line has none.

### `tableStart?`

```kex
tableStart?(lines: [String]) -> Bool
```

--- tables ------------------------------------------------------------

Returns `true` when the lines start a GFM table: a header row followed by a row of dashes. Without that row the lines are a paragraph.

### `delimiterRow?`

```kex
delimiterRow?(line: String) -> Bool
```

### `delimiterChar?`

```kex
delimiterChar?(c: String) -> Bool
```

### `takeTable`

```kex
takeTable(lines: [String]) -> (MdBlock, [String])
```

### `cellsOf`

```kex
cellsOf(line: String) -> [String]
```

Returns the cells of a table row. Leading and trailing pipes are optional.

### `takeParagraph`

```kex
takeParagraph(lines: [String]) -> (MdBlock, [String])
```

--- paragraphs --------------------------------------------------------

Takes a paragraph, which ends at a blank line or where another block starts, so a list or code fence right under prose is not swallowed.

### `paragraphLine?`

```kex
paragraphLine?(line: String) -> Bool
```

### `render`

```kex
render(items: [MdBlock]) -> String
```

--- rendering ---------------------------------------------------------

### `renderBlock`

```kex
renderBlock(block: MdBlock) -> String
```

### `renderCode`

```kex
renderCode(language: String, body: String) -> String
```

Renders a code block. Kex code goes through the reference pages' highlighter; other languages are escaped and left plain.

### `renderItems`

```kex
renderItems(items: [ListItem]) -> String
```

### `renderItem`

```kex
renderItem(item: ListItem) -> String
```

### `renderTable`

```kex
renderTable(header: [String], rows: [[String]]) -> String
```

### `renderRow`

```kex
renderRow(row: [String]) -> String
```

### `anchor`

```kex
anchor(text: String) -> String
```

Returns a heading's id: lower case, with each run of characters other than letters and digits turned into one dash.

### `trimDashes`

```kex
trimDashes(text: String) -> String
```

Removes dashes from both ends, which `anchor` can leave: `(try)` becomes `-try-` before this.

### `anchorChar`

```kex
anchorChar(c: Char) -> String
```

### `squeezeDashes`

```kex
squeezeDashes(text: String, accum: String) -> String
```

### `stripInline`

```kex
stripInline(text: String) -> String
```

Returns the text with the inline markers (backticks, `*` and `_`) removed.

### `inline`

```kex
inline(text: String) -> String
```

--- inline ------------------------------------------------------------

Renders inline Markdown. Code spans are handled first: their content is escaped but not scanned for emphasis, so `a*b*c` in backticks stays as written.

### `inlineLoop`

```kex
inlineLoop(text: String, accum: String) -> String
```

### `emphasis`

```kex
emphasis(text: String) -> String
```

Renders links, then bold and italics, so a `*` inside a URL is not read as a marker.

### `links`

```kex
links(text: String, accum: String) -> String
```

### `linkParts`

```kex
linkParts(rest: String) -> (String, String, String)?
```

Splits `label](href)` and what follows it into `(label, href, rest)`, or returns `None` when it is not a link, and the `[` is plain text.

### `marks`

```kex
marks(text: String) -> String
```

Renders bold before italics, or the opening `**` would be read as empty italics. The remaining text is escaped here.

### `wrap`

```kex
wrap(text: String, strongMark: String, strongTag: String, emMark: String, emTag: String) -> String
```

### `pairs`

```kex
pairs(text: String, mark: String, tag: String, accum: String) -> String
```

Replaces each pair of markers with a tag. A marker without a partner is left as written.

### `indexOfText`

```kex
indexOfText(haystack: String, needle: String, at: Integer) -> Integer?
```

Returns where `needle` first occurs in `haystack` from `at` on, or `None`. `String.indexOf` only finds a `Char`, and `**` is two characters.

### `esc`

```kex
esc(s: String) -> String
```

## record `Frontmatter`

The frontmatter keys this reader uses. Other keys are ignored, so a page may carry metadata for something else.

**Fields**

  - `title` : [String](../../../../prelude/0.4.0-rc.5-dev/string.md#make-string) (optional)
  - `description` : [String](../../../../prelude/0.4.0-rc.5-dev/string.md#make-string) (optional)
  - `order` : [Integer](../../../../prelude/0.4.0-rc.5-dev/number.md#make-integer) (optional)



## record `ListItem`

One item of a list: its own inline text, plus any blocks nested under it.

**Fields**

  - `text` : [String](../../../../prelude/0.4.0-rc.5-dev/string.md#make-string)
  - `children` : [[MdBlock](#type-tey-docgen-md-mdblock)]



## type `MdBlock`

A block of a Markdown document.

**Variants**

  - `Heading(Integer, String)`
  - `Paragraph(String)`
  - `Code(String, String)`
  - `Quote([MdBlock])`
  - `Bullets([ListItem])`
  - `Numbers([ListItem])`
  - `Table([String], [[String]])`
  - `Rule`



## record `Document`

A parsed document: its frontmatter and its blocks.

**Fields**

  - `frontmatter` : [Frontmatter](#record-tey-docgen-md-frontmatter)
  - `blocks` : [[MdBlock](#type-tey-docgen-md-mdblock)]

package: tey
version: "0.2.1-dev"

title: Tey.Docgen.Model
entities:
  - { kind: module, name: "Tey.Docgen.Model" }
---

# Tey.Docgen.Model

The records `tey docs` extracts from source, from which the Markdown, the JSON and the search index are all produced.

No field is called `type`, because `type` after a dot is read as a keyword. The JSON key names are chosen in `Tey.Docgen.Json`.

## module `Tey.Docgen.Model`

### `emptyDoc`

```kex
emptyDoc -> Doc
```

### `kindOf`

```kex
kindOf(entity: Entity) -> String
```

Returns the kind label an entity has in indexes and JSON, such as `"record"` or `"make"`.

### `nameOf`

```kex
nameOf(entity: Entity) -> String
```

Returns an entity's display name; a make's is its target type.

### `qualifiedNameOf`

```kex
qualifiedNameOf(entity: Entity) -> String
```

### `lineOf`

```kex
lineOf(entity: Entity) -> Integer
```

### `anchorOf`

```kex
anchorOf(entity: Entity) -> String
```

Returns the id of an entity's HTML section.

It is here, not in the HTML renderer, because the cross-link index and the sidebar need the same ids.

### `anchorNameOf`

```kex
anchorNameOf(entity: Entity) -> String
```

Returns the text an entity's anchor is made from: a make's full target, type parameters included, or otherwise the qualified name.

### `memberAnchorOf`

```kex
memberAnchorOf(owner: String, name: String) -> String
```

Returns the anchor of a function documented inside a trait or make section. It includes the owner, because one page can hold several owners with a `count`, such as `[X]` and `String`.

### `ownerSlugOf`

```kex
ownerSlugOf(owner: String) -> String
```

Returns the slug of an owner type: `[X]` gives "list", `[Number]` gives "list-number" and `FileHandle<CanRead, W>` gives "filehandle-canread". Type variables (a capital letter, optionally followed by a digit) are dropped.

### `typeVariable?`

```kex
typeVariable?(word: String) -> Bool
```

### `wordsOf`

```kex
wordsOf(text: String) -> [String]
```

Returns the runs of letters, digits, `_`, `?` and `!` in a type's text.

### `wordSplit`

```kex
wordSplit(rest: String, word: String, out: [String]) -> [String]
```

### `slugOf`

```kex
slugOf(name: String) -> String
```

Returns a name spelled for an HTML id: lower case, with each run of punctuation turned into one dash. `?` and `!` are kept, as in `empty?`.

### `operatorSlug`

```kex
operatorSlug(name: String) -> String
```

Returns the slug of an operator, which has no letters of its own: `<=>` gives "op-lt-eq-gt" and a plus sign "op-plus".

### `operatorCharName`

```kex
operatorCharName(c: Char) -> String
```

### `baseTypeOf`

```kex
baseTypeOf(target: String) -> String
```

Returns the type a make block extends, without its type arguments: "[X]" gives "List", "{K: V}" and "Map<K, V>" give "Map", and "FileHandle<R, W>" gives "FileHandle".

  - `line` : [Integer](../../../../prelude/0.4.0-rc.5-dev/number.md#make-integer)

## record `Extension`

One `make` block as seen from the type it extends: where it is, the names it adds and the traits it declares.

A type's functions can be spread over many files (there is a `make Integer` in number.kex, period.kex, units.kex and others), and these rows gather them on the type's page.

**Fields**

  - `target` : [String](../../../../prelude/0.4.0-rc.5-dev/string.md#make-string)
  - `urlPath` : [String](../../../../prelude/0.4.0-rc.5-dev/string.md#make-string)
  - `pageTitle` : [String](../../../../prelude/0.4.0-rc.5-dev/string.md#make-string)
  - `anchor` : [String](../../../../prelude/0.4.0-rc.5-dev/string.md#make-string)
  - `implements` : [[String](../../../../prelude/0.4.0-rc.5-dev/string.md#make-string)]
  - `names` : [[String](../../../../prelude/0.4.0-rc.5-dev/string.md#make-string)]



## record `TypeFacts`

Everything the package says about one type, across files.

`homePath` is the type's main page: the one declaring it, or for a builtin such as Integer or String the one named after it.

**Fields**

  - `name` : [String](../../../../prelude/0.4.0-rc.5-dev/string.md#make-string)
  - `homePath` : [String](../../../../prelude/0.4.0-rc.5-dev/string.md#make-string)
  - `homeAnchor` : [String](../../../../prelude/0.4.0-rc.5-dev/string.md#make-string)
  - `extensions` : [[Extension](#record-tey-docgen-model-extension)]
  - `traits` : [[String](../../../../prelude/0.4.0-rc.5-dev/string.md#make-string)]



## record `TraitFacts`

A trait seen from the outside: where it is documented and which make blocks implement it.

**Fields**

  - `name` : [String](../../../../prelude/0.4.0-rc.5-dev/string.md#make-string)
  - `qualifiedName` : [String](../../../../prelude/0.4.0-rc.5-dev/string.md#make-string)
  - `urlPath` : [String](../../../../prelude/0.4.0-rc.5-dev/string.md#make-string)
  - `anchor` : [String](../../../../prelude/0.4.0-rc.5-dev/string.md#make-string)
  - `implementors` : [[Extension](#record-tey-docgen-model-extension)]



## record `ModuleIndexEntry`

One module of the package and the page its entities are on.

The sidebar and the module index of model.json are built from these. Readers navigate by module, and a module need not match a file.

**Fields**

  - `qualifiedName` : [String](../../../../prelude/0.4.0-rc.5-dev/string.md#make-string)
  - `summary` : [String](../../../../prelude/0.4.0-rc.5-dev/string.md#make-string)
  - `urlPath` : [String](../../../../prelude/0.4.0-rc.5-dev/string.md#make-string)
  - `members` : [[MemberEntry](#record-tey-docgen-model-memberentry)]



## record `MemberEntry`

One documented member of a module and the anchor of its section, for the sidebar and the JSON index.

**Fields**

  - `name` : [String](../../../../prelude/0.4.0-rc.5-dev/string.md#make-string)
  - `anchor` : [String](../../../../prelude/0.4.0-rc.5-dev/string.md#make-string)



## record `LinkEntry`

One row of the cross-link index: a name that a type reference may mention, such as "String" or "FS.Path", and where it links to. Every renderer resolves names against this one list.

**Fields**

  - `name` : [String](../../../../prelude/0.4.0-rc.5-dev/string.md#make-string)
  - `urlPath` : [String](../../../../prelude/0.4.0-rc.5-dev/string.md#make-string)
  - `anchor` : [String](../../../../prelude/0.4.0-rc.5-dev/string.md#make-string)
  - `kind` : [String](../../../../prelude/0.4.0-rc.5-dev/string.md#make-string)



## record `PackageModel`

Everything extracted from one package: its pages, modules, links and cross-file relations.

**Fields**

  - `package` : [String](../../../../prelude/0.4.0-rc.5-dev/string.md#make-string)
  - `version` : [String](../../../../prelude/0.4.0-rc.5-dev/string.md#make-string)
  - `label` : [String](../../../../prelude/0.4.0-rc.5-dev/string.md#make-string)
  - `baseUrl` : [String](../../../../prelude/0.4.0-rc.5-dev/string.md#make-string)
  - `generatedAt` : [String](../../../../prelude/0.4.0-rc.5-dev/string.md#make-string)

  - `modules` : [[ModuleIndexEntry](#record-tey-docgen-model-moduleindexentry)] (optional)
  - `links` : [[LinkEntry](#record-tey-docgen-model-linkentry)] (optional)
  - `preludeModules` : [[String](../../../../prelude/0.4.0-rc.5-dev/string.md#make-string)] (optional)
  - `preludeSource` : [String](../../../../prelude/0.4.0-rc.5-dev/string.md#make-string) (optional)

  - `traits` : [[TraitFacts](#record-tey-docgen-model-traitfacts)] (optional)



## record `SearchEntry`

One row of the search index, for an entity or for a function inside a trait, make or module.

`types` are the type names its signature mentions, so a search can match by type as well as by name. `anchor` is the section a result links to.

  - `urlPath` : [String](../../../../prelude/0.4.0-rc.5-dev/string.md#make-string)
  - `anchor` : [String](../../../../prelude/0.4.0-rc.5-dev/string.md#make-string) (optional)
  - `line` : [Integer](../../../../prelude/0.4.0-rc.5-dev/number.md#make-integer)

  - `generatedAt` : [String](../../../../prelude/0.4.0-rc.5-dev/string.md#make-string)

package: tey
version: "0.2.1-dev"

title: Tey.Docgen.Nav
entities:
  - { kind: module, name: "Tey.Docgen.Nav" }
---

# Tey.Docgen.Nav

Navigation and cross-linking: the two indexes every renderer uses, built once from the extracted pages.

```kex
modules: one ModuleIndexEntry per module, for the sidebar
links:   one LinkEntry per linkable name
```

Building them in one place means the HTML, the Markdown and model.json always agree on where a name links to.

## module `Tey.Docgen.Nav`

### `buildModules`

```kex
buildModules(pages: [SourcePage]) -> [ModuleIndexEntry]
```

Returns an entry for every module in the package, in declaration order, with the page it is on. Nested modules get entries of their own.

### `modulesOnPage`

```kex
modulesOnPage(entities: [Entity], urlPath: String) -> [ModuleIndexEntry]
```

### `moduleEntry`

```kex
moduleEntry(entry: ModuleEntry, urlPath: String) -> ModuleIndexEntry
```

### `firstLine`

```kex
firstLine(summary: String) -> String
```

### `parentTitleOf`

```kex
parentTitleOf(pages: [SourcePage], page: SourcePage) -> String?
```

Returns the title of the page that `page` nests under, or `None` for a top-level page.

The parent is found from titles, not paths: "Net.DNS" nests under "Net", and "Net.HTTP.WebSocket" under "Net.HTTP". The longest prefix that has a page wins. When no prefix has a page ("Control" for "Control.Retry"), the page is top-level.

### `parentLoop`

```kex
parentLoop(parts: [String], pages: [SourcePage], page: SourcePage) -> String?
```

### `claimedByAnother?`

```kex
claimedByAnother?(pages: [SourcePage], page: SourcePage, title: String) -> Bool
```

### `topLevelPages`

```kex
topLevelPages(pages: [SourcePage]) -> [SourcePage]
```

Returns the pages with no parent, sorted by title, for the sidebar's top level.

### `childPages`

```kex
childPages(pages: [SourcePage], title: String) -> [SourcePage]
```

Returns the pages nested directly under `title`, sorted by title.

### `descendantPages`

```kex
descendantPages(pages: [SourcePage], page: SourcePage) -> [SourcePage]
```

Returns every page nested under `page` at any depth, sorted by title. A module page lists these as its submodules.

### `sortedByTitle`

```kex
sortedByTitle(pages: [SourcePage]) -> [SourcePage]
```

### `buildLinks`

```kex
buildLinks(pages: [SourcePage]) -> [LinkEntry]
```

Returns the names that can be linked, each with its page and anchor.

A name links only while exactly one place answers to it. A qualified name ("FS.Path") is usually unique; a simple one ("Path") stops linking as soon as two different entities share it, and then only the qualified names link.

### `withTypeHomes`

```kex
withTypeHomes(links: [LinkEntry], types: [Tey.Docgen.Model.TypeFacts]) -> [LinkEntry]
```

Returns `links` plus a link to the home page of each type that make blocks extend and that does not link yet.

A name such as `Integer` is claimed by a module and by several make blocks, so `buildLinks` drops it. In a signature it means the type, which has a home page (`Relations.homePathOf`), so this adds that link. A name that already links keeps its link.

### `linkEntriesOnPage`

```kex
linkEntriesOnPage(entities: [Entity], urlPath: String) -> [LinkEntry]
```

### `memberLinks`

```kex
memberLinks(ownerName: String, owner: String, functions: [Tey.Docgen.Model.FunctionEntry], urlPath: String) -> [LinkEntry]
```

Returns links for the functions of a trait or make block under their owner's name, so prose that writes `List.map` links to that function.

### `linkableNames`

```kex
linkableNames(e: Entity) -> [String]
```

Returns the names an entity can be linked under: its qualified name and its simple name. Functions have none of their own. A make block links under its target's base name, so "Map<K, V>" links as "Map"; a list target such as "[X]" does not link.

### `uniqueTarget?`

```kex
uniqueTarget?(entries: [LinkEntry], candidate: LinkEntry) -> Bool
```

Returns `true` when every entry with `candidate`'s name points at the same page and anchor.

### `differentTarget?`

```kex
differentTarget?(a: LinkEntry, b: LinkEntry) -> Bool
```

### `resolve`

```kex
resolve(links: [LinkEntry], name: String) -> LinkEntry?
```

### `segmentsOf`

```kex
segmentsOf(typeText: String) -> [String]
```

Splits a type reference into identifiers and the separators between them, so a renderer can link the identifiers: "Map<String, FS.Path>" gives ["Map", "<", "String", ", ", "FS.Path", ">"].

### `splitLoop`

```kex
splitLoop(rest: String, ident: String, sep: String, out: [String]) -> [String]
```

`ident` is the identifier being read, `sep` the separator run since it; only one is non-empty at a time, and whichever it is goes out in order.

### `flushIdent`

```kex
flushIdent(ident: String, out: [String]) -> [String]
```

### `flushSep`

```kex
flushSep(sep: String, out: [String]) -> [String]
```

### `isIdentChar?`

```kex
isIdentChar?(ch: String) -> Bool
```

### `hrefFrom`

```kex
hrefFrom(fromPath: String, toPath: String, anchor: String) -> String
```

Returns the relative href from one page of the package to an anchor on another: "#anchor" on the same page, otherwise a path up to the version directory and down to the target.

### `upsToVersionDir`

```kex
upsToVersionDir(urlPath: String) -> String
```

### `ups`

```kex
ups(n: Integer) -> String
```

package: tey
version: "0.2.1-dev"

  - { kind: module, name: "Tey.Docgen.Prose" }

# Tey.Docgen.Prose

`tey docs prose`: renders a tree of Markdown files as a site, with the same layout as the generated reference.

A prose site belongs to a named, versioned unit, as a reference build does, so the two can sit side by side in one site and share `versions.json`, the stylesheet and the layout. `build` derives its pages from `.kex` sources; `prose` renders them from `.md` files.

The command does not care what the prose is: a guide, a book and a package's handbook are all treated the same. Naming the units and putting several of them together into one site is left to the caller.

## module `Tey.Docgen.Prose`

### `proseCommand` (foul)

```kex
proseCommand(parsed: ParsedOptions) -> Integer
```

### `readPages` (foul)

```kex
readPages(files: [String], source: String, accum: [ProsePage]) -> [ProsePage]
```

### `pageOf`

```kex
pageOf(fileName: String, text: String) -> ProsePage
```

### `stripSuffix`

```kex
stripSuffix(name: String, suffix: String) -> String
```

### `writeProse` (foul)

```kex
writeProse(pages: [ProsePage], versionDir: String, out: String, model: PackageModel) -> ()
```

Writes each page as HTML and as Markdown side by side, as reference builds do, plus the index page and the shared assets.

### `writeProseLoop` (foul)

```kex
writeProseLoop(pages: [ProsePage], index: Integer, versionDir: String, model: PackageModel) -> ()
```

### `proseIndexHtml`

```kex
proseIndexHtml(pages: [ProsePage], model: PackageModel) -> String
```

Renders the index page: the chapters in the author's order, each with its description. Reference builds use `versionIndexHtml`, a grid of modules, instead; the two are kept separate so book layout never reaches `tey docs build`.

### `chapterItem`

```kex
chapterItem(prose: ProsePage) -> String
```

### `prevNextHtml`

```kex
prevNextHtml(pages: [ProsePage], index: Integer) -> String
```

Renders a chapter's footer: links to the previous and next chapters. The first and last chapters get only one link.

### `prevLink`

```kex
prevLink(pages: [ProsePage], index: Integer, up: String) -> String
```

### `nextLink`

```kex
nextLink(pages: [ProsePage], index: Integer, up: String) -> String
```

### `chapterNav`

```kex
chapterNav(prev: String, nextHtml: String) -> String
```

## record `ProsePage`

One Markdown page, read and rendered: its place in the site, its sort order and description from the frontmatter, its HTML, and the Markdown without frontmatter that is served as its `.md` version.

**Fields**

  - `page` : [SourcePage](../../tey/docgen/model.md#record-tey-docgen-model-sourcepage)
  - `order` : [Integer](../../../../prelude/0.4.0-rc.5-dev/number.md#make-integer)
  - `body` : [String](../../../../prelude/0.4.0-rc.5-dev/string.md#make-string)
  - `description` : [String](../../../../prelude/0.4.0-rc.5-dev/string.md#make-string)
  - `markdown` : [String](../../../../prelude/0.4.0-rc.5-dev/string.md#make-string)

package: tey
version: "0.2.1-dev"
source: tey/docgen/rdoc.kex
title: Tey.Docgen.Rdoc
entities:
  - { kind: module, name: "Tey.Docgen.Rdoc" }
---

# Tey.Docgen.Rdoc

Parses the text of an RDoc-style doc comment into a `Tey.Docgen.Model.Doc` record.

A doc comment is prose followed by directive lines:

```kex
# Sums all elements. Returns +0+ for an empty list.
#
# @param f [X -> Number] maps each element
# @return [Number]
# @example
#   [1, 2].sum   # => 3
```

In prose, a word or phrase between two plus signs becomes Markdown inline code.

## module `Tey.Docgen.Rdoc`

### `parseDoc`

```kex
parseDoc(text: String) -> Doc?
```

Parses a doc comment's text, or returns `None` for empty text.

### `parseOrEmpty`

```kex
parseOrEmpty(text: String) -> Doc
```

Parses a doc comment's text, giving an empty `Doc` for empty text.

### `rewriteProseBlocks`

```kex
rewriteProseBlocks(blocks: [[String]]) -> [[String]]
```

Rewrites plus-sign code markup in each prose block separately, leaving verbatim blocks and `@example` code alone. `@param` and `@return` descriptions are prose and are rewritten.

A pair never spans two blocks. Rewriting the whole comment at once would pair the plus sign of an addition in a code sample with the next markup in the prose.

### `rewriteProseBlock`

```kex
rewriteProseBlock(block: [String]) -> [String]
```

### `rewritePlusPairs`

```kex
rewritePlusPairs(s: String, accum: String) -> String
```

### `plusPair?`

```kex
plusPair?(head: String, inner: String, tail: String) -> Bool
```

Returns `true` when a pair of plus signs around `inner` is markup. There must be no space just inside either sign, so an addition with spaces stays as written; no backtick inside, so spans never nest; and no letter or digit just outside, so an addition without spaces stays too.

### `boundaryBefore?`

```kex
boundaryBefore?(head: String) -> Bool
```

### `boundaryAfter?`

```kex
boundaryAfter?(tail: String) -> Bool
```

### `splitParagraphs`

```kex
splitParagraphs(lines: [String], current: [String], accum: [[String]]) -> [[String]]
```

Splits lines into blocks. Prose runs until a blank line. Every line that starts with `@` opens a block of its own, so consecutive `@param` lines stay separate, and the indented lines after a directive (an example's code) belong to it.

### `directiveBlock?`

```kex
directiveBlock?(current: [String]) -> Bool
```

### `indented?`

```kex
indented?(line: String) -> Bool
```

### `indentWidth`

```kex
indentWidth(s: String) -> Integer
```

Returns the number of leading spaces in a line.

### `verbatim?`

```kex
verbatim?(lines: [String]) -> Bool
```

Returns `true` for a verbatim block: one whose every non-blank line is indented by at least two spaces, as RDoc marks code or a hand-laid-out table. Such a block keeps its line breaks and is carried into the summary as a fenced code block.

### `dedent`

```kex
dedent(lines: [String]) -> [String]
```

Removes the indentation shared by every non-blank line, so a block renders flush left.

### `fenceVerbatim`

```kex
fenceVerbatim(lines: [String]) -> String
```

### `mergeVerbatim`

```kex
mergeVerbatim(blocks: [[String]], accum: [[String]]) -> [[String]]
```

Joins adjacent verbatim blocks back together with a blank line between them, since a blank line inside a code sample does not end it.

### `classifyBlocks`

```kex
classifyBlocks(blocks: [[String]], summary: String, params: [Param], returns: Return?, examples: [Example], deprecated: String?) -> Doc?
```

### `directiveBody`

```kex
directiveBody(lines: [String], prefixLength: Integer) -> String
```

### `parseParam`

```kex
parseParam(lines: [String]) -> Param
```

Reads a `@param name [Type] description` directive.

### `parseReturn`

```kex
parseReturn(lines: [String]) -> Return
```

Reads a `@return [Type] description` directive.

### `parseExample`

```kex
parseExample(lines: [String]) -> Example
```

### `parseBracketed`

```kex
parseBracketed(s: String) -> Bracketed?
```

Splits text that opens with a bracketed group, such as `[Integer] the count`, into the group's content and the rest. Returns `None` when the text does not open with one.

### `findClosingBracket`

```kex
findClosingBracket(s: String, index: Integer, depth: Integer) -> Integer?
```

## record `Bracketed`

**Fields**

  - `content` : [String](../../../../prelude/0.4.0-rc.5-dev/string.md#make-string)
  - `rest` : [String](../../../../prelude/0.4.0-rc.5-dev/string.md#make-string)

package: tey
version: "0.2.1-dev"
source: tey/docgen/relations.kex
title: Tey.Docgen.Relations
entities:
  - { kind: module, name: "Tey.Docgen.Relations" }
---

# Tey.Docgen.Relations

Relations across files: which make blocks extend which type, which traits a type implements, and which types implement each trait.

Extraction works one file at a time, but readers look things up by type. The functions on `Integer` are spread over number.kex, period.kex, units.kex and algebra.kex, and that a `List` is `Enumerable`, and so has `map`, `filter` and `find`, is written on a make block rather than on the type. These indexes let the List page say where its functions come from, and the Enumerable page list its implementors.

## module `Tey.Docgen.Relations`

### `build`

```kex
build(pages: [SourcePage]) -> ([TypeFacts], [TraitFacts])
```

### `withTraitSignatures`

```kex
withTraitSignatures(pages: [SourcePage]) -> [SourcePage]
```

Returns `pages` with each untyped make member that implements a trait function given the trait's signature.

For `let identity = 0` under `make Integer, implement: Monoid`, that is the signature `Monoid` declares, with `This` read as `Integer`. It runs on the pages before anything renders them, so every output shows the same signature.

### `typedByTraits`

```kex
typedByTraits(e: Entity, traits: [TraitEntry]) -> Entity
```

### `typedByTrait`

```kex
typedByTrait(f: FunctionEntry, m: MakeEntry, traits: [TraitEntry]) -> FunctionEntry
```

### `asImplementor`

```kex
asImplementor(signature: String, target: String) -> String
```

### `pageExtensions`

```kex
pageExtensions(page: SourcePage, entities: [Entity]) -> [Extension]
```

### `extensionOf`

```kex
extensionOf(page: SourcePage, entity: Entity, entry: MakeEntry) -> Extension
```

### `typeFacts`

```kex
typeFacts(base: String, extensions: [Extension], pages: [SourcePage]) -> TypeFacts
```

### `homePathOf`

```kex
homePathOf(base: String, mine: [Extension], pages: [SourcePage]) -> String
```

Returns the page a type's links should go to.

That is the page declaring the type; failing that, the page titled after it (string.kex for the built-in String); then a page with both the type's companion module and a make block for it; and last the page whose make block adds the most functions, so number.kex for Integer rather than algebra.kex, which only makes it a Monoid.

### `homeAnchorOf`

```kex
homeAnchorOf(base: String, home: String, mine: [Extension], pages: [SourcePage]) -> String
```

### `declarationAnchors`

```kex
declarationAnchors(entities: [Entity], base: String) -> [String]
```

### `companionModule?`

```kex
companionModule?(entities: [Entity], base: String) -> Bool
```

### `declares?`

```kex
declares?(entities: [Entity], base: String) -> Bool
```

### `pageTraits`

```kex
pageTraits(page: SourcePage, entities: [Entity], extensions: [Extension]) -> [TraitFacts]
```

### `namesTrait?`

```kex
namesTrait?(written: String, name: String, qualifiedName: String) -> Bool
```

Returns whether `written`, as it appears in an `implement:` list, names the trait `name`. `implement: Enumerable` and `implement: Kex.Enumerable` both name the trait declared as `Enumerable` inside `module Kex`.

### `typeFactsFor`

```kex
typeFactsFor(model: PackageModel, base: String) -> TypeFacts?
```

Returns the facts for the type that make target `base` extends, or `None` when no make block extends it.

### `traitFactsFor`

```kex
traitFactsFor(model: PackageModel, written: String) -> TraitFacts?
```

### `traitEntryFor`

```kex
traitEntryFor(model: PackageModel, facts: TraitFacts) -> TraitEntry?
```

Returns the declaration of a trait, for its list of functions.

### `traitEntries`

```kex
traitEntries(entities: [Entity]) -> [TraitEntry]
```

### `traitMethods`

```kex
traitMethods(model: PackageModel, entry: TraitEntry) -> ([FunctionEntry], [FunctionEntry])
```

Returns a trait's functions as an implementor sees them: the required ones and the provided ones.

A function is required when the trait gives it no body and no `make <Trait>` block in any file gives it a default. The provided ones are the rest, plus any functions such a block adds that the trait does not declare.

### `traitDefaults`

```kex
traitDefaults(entities: [Entity], entry: TraitEntry) -> [FunctionEntry]
```

### `traitTarget?`

```kex
traitTarget?(model: PackageModel, target: String) -> Bool
```

Returns whether a make target names a trait of this package.

### `allFunctions`

```kex
allFunctions(entities: [Entity]) -> [FunctionEntry]
```

Returns every function documented in `entities`: top-level and module functions, trait functions and make members.

### `required?`

```kex
required?(f: FunctionEntry) -> Bool
```

Returns whether a trait function has no body, so an implementor must write it.

# Tey.Docgen.Scan

Finds the files a docs build reads by walking a source tree.

Paths come back relative to the root, sorted within each directory. `spec/` directories and `.spec.kex` files are skipped: specs cover the same declarations as the file they test, so pages for them would repeat every entry.

## module `Tey.Docgen.Scan`

### `sourceFiles` (foul)

```kex
sourceFiles(sourceDir: String) -> [String]
```

### `proseFiles` (foul)

```kex
proseFiles(sourceDir: String) -> [String]
```

Returns the `.md` files under `sourceDir` that `tey docs prose` reads, found by the same walk as the `.kex` sources.

### `filesWithSuffix` (foul)

```kex
filesWithSuffix(sourceDir: String, suffix: String) -> [String]
```

### `subdirectories` (foul)

```kex
subdirectories(sourceDir: String) -> [String]
```

### `nested` (foul)

```kex
nested(dirs: [String], sourceDir: String, suffix: String) -> [String]
```

# Tey.Docgen.Serve

`tey docs serve`: serves a generated site from its output directory over HTTP on localhost.

## module `Tey.Docgen.Serve`

### `serveCommand` (foul)

```kex
serveCommand(parsed: ParsedOptions) -> Integer
```

### `routesFor`

```kex
routesFor(prefix: String, name: String) -> [String]
```

Returns the URL paths that serve a file. The router matches paths exactly, so an index.html gets three: its own path, its directory, and its directory with a trailing slash. Any other file gets only its own path.

### `collectServeFiles` (foul)

```kex
collectServeFiles(dir: String, prefix: String) -> [ServedFile]
```

### `serveFile` (foul)

```kex
serveFile(filePath: String, _request: Request<Binary>, _context: Context) -> Response<Binary>
```

Serves the file at `filePath`; `~serveFile(path)` is a route handler. The file is read as bytes, so images and fonts are served intact, and the response says `no-cache` because the site is rebuilt in place.

### `contentTypeFor`

```kex
contentTypeFor(path: String) -> String
```

## record `ServedFile`

**Fields**

  - `route` : [String](../../../../prelude/0.4.0-rc.5-dev/string.md#make-string)
  - `path` : [String](../../../../prelude/0.4.0-rc.5-dev/string.md#make-string)
